name: hastebin-ansi
author: freelance@harrydev.me
description: Hastebin paste server with ANSI color support and an MCP endpoint for AI assistants. The server image is built by GitHub Actions. The default image is a fixed release; pick the newer release image in Startup to update, or "latest (follows main)" to get every change on restart. The install script only writes config.yaml and creates the data folder.

installation.script:
#!/bin/ash
# hastebin-ansi install script.
# Nothing is compiled here: the server binary ships in the Docker image,
# which GitHub Actions builds. This only prepares the server folder.
set -e
cd /mnt/server

DATA_DIR="${STORAGE_FILE_PATH:-data}"

# Remove leftovers of the old egg, which built from source.
# Only these exact names are removed. The data dir is never touched.
for f in hastebin hastebin-ansi static cmd config handler internal .github .git \
    go.mod go.sum Dockerfile .dockerignore .gitignore docker-compose.yaml docker-compose.yml \
    README.md LICENSE about.md config.yaml.example config.example.yaml; do
    if [ "$f" = "$DATA_DIR" ] || [ "$f" = "data" ]; then
        continue
    fi
    if [ -e "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ]; then
        echo "Removing old build file: $f"
        rm -rf "./$f"
    fi
done

# Keep the previous config as a backup, never overwriting an older backup
if [ -f config.yaml ]; then
    BACKUP="config.yaml.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
    echo "Saving the old config.yaml as $BACKUP"
    mv config.yaml "$BACKUP"
fi

# Fresh config. Egg variables (environment) override these values at startup.
cat > config.yaml <<'EOF'
host: "0.0.0.0"
port: 7777
key_length: 16
max_length: 33554432
# Memory that reads and large uploads may hold at the same time
memory_budget: 268435456
# Bytes one client may upload per hour
upload_quota: 268435456
# Paste lifetime in seconds, 0 means pastes never expire.
# With file storage, files older than this are deleted.
expiration: 0
key_generator: "phonetic"
base_url: "https://paste.superkali.me"
mcp_enable: true
max_concurrent_uploads: 8
max_uploads_per_ip: 1
upload_timeout: 300

storage:
  type: "file"
  file_path: "data"

documents:
  - key: "about"
    path: "/opt/hastebin/about.md"

rate_limiting:
  enable: true
  limit: 500
  window: 15

logging:
  level: "info"
  colorize: false
EOF

mkdir -p data
echo "Install done. The server binary comes from the Docker image."

variables.name: Storage Type
variables.description: Where pastes are stored: file, redis, memcached, mongodb, postgres or s3.

variables.name: Storage File Path
variables.description: Folder for pastes when Storage Type is file, relative to the server folder.

variables.name: Key Length
variables.description: Length of the paste keys in the URL, at least 12, so keys cannot be guessed.

variables.name: Expiration
variables.description: Paste lifetime in seconds, 0 means pastes never expire. Each read starts it again. With file storage, a value above 0 deletes every paste file not read or written for that long, existing pastes included. S3 storage ignores it. On a public server set it, for example 2592000 (30 days), so the disk does not fill up.

variables.name: Max Length
variables.description: Largest paste accepted, in bytes. 33554432 is 32 MiB. With file storage, uploads and reads are streamed to and from disk through small buffers. Other storage types hold whole pastes in memory and are capped at 8 MiB.

variables.name: Max Concurrent Uploads
variables.description: Large uploads (over 1 MiB) received at the same time. More are refused with 503 until a slot frees up. -1 means no limit.

variables.name: Max Uploads Per IP
variables.description: Large uploads (over 1 MiB) one client may send at the same time. An IPv6 client counts as its whole /64. More are refused with 503. -1 means no limit.

variables.name: Max Requests Per Client
variables.description: Requests one client may have in progress at the same time, on all routes together, web page files included. More get 429. An IPv6 client counts as its whole /64. -1 means no limit.

variables.name: MCP Max Requests Per Client
variables.description: Requests to /mcp one client may have in progress at the same time. More get 429. -1 means no limit.

variables.name: Upload Timeout
variables.description: Seconds an upload may take to arrive and be answered. Uploads slower than 64 KiB per 10 seconds are dropped earlier, and so is an upload that has run for a minute and averaged less than 64 KiB per second. -1 keeps the 60 second server timeout.

variables.name: Memory Budget
variables.description: Memory, in bytes, that paste reads and uploads may hold at the same time, half for each. 268435456 is 256 MiB. Requests that do not fit get 503 and are retried, and one client may hold at most an eighth of it. The server uses at most 40 percent of its memory limit for it and keeps the rest for itself and the kernel, so give it 640 MiB of RAM or more to keep 256 MiB. With less RAM it uses 40 percent of the limit instead.

variables.name: Minimum Free Disk
variables.description: Bytes that must stay free on the disk of the data folder (file storage only). An upload that would leave less gets 507. 1073741824 is 1 GiB. -1 turns the check off.

variables.name: Upload Quota
variables.description: Bytes one client may upload per hour, so nobody can fill the disk. 268435456 is 256 MiB. An IPv6 client counts as its whole /64. Over it uploads get 429. -1 turns it off.

variables.name: Key Generator
variables.description: How paste keys are made: phonetic (easy to read) or random.

variables.name: Logging Level
variables.description: How much the server logs.

variables.name: Rate Limit Enable
variables.description: Limit the number of requests per client IP.

variables.name: Rate Limit Requests
variables.description: Requests allowed per client IP in each window.

variables.name: Rate Limit Window
variables.description: Length of the rate limit window, in seconds.

variables.name: Trusted Proxies
variables.description: Comma separated IPs or CIDRs of the reverse proxy allowed to pass the real client IP. With cloudflared on the host this is the Docker gateway (172.18.0.1): then bind the allocation to 127.0.0.1, so nothing else can come in through the gateway. With cloudflared in a container, give it a fixed IP and list that instead. Leave empty to ignore client IP headers.

variables.name: Real IP Header
variables.description: Header that carries the client IP from the trusted proxy: CF-Connecting-IP for cloudflared, X-Real-IP, or X-Forwarded-For.

variables.name: Base URL
variables.description: Public URL of the server, used in the links that /log and MCP return, for example https://paste.example.com. Without it links would follow the Host header the client sends.

variables.name: Metrics Address
variables.description: Address for a separate Prometheus metrics listener, for example 127.0.0.1:9100. Leave empty to turn metrics off.

variables.name: MCP Enable
variables.description: Serve the MCP endpoint at /mcp, so AI assistants can upload and read pastes. The web page shows how to add it.

variables.name: MCP Max Length
variables.description: Largest text the MCP upload_log tool accepts, in bytes. 4194304 is 4 MiB, 0 means that default. Decoding the JSON takes about 6 times the request size, so it is never more than Max Length, nor more than fits, 6 times over, in what one client may hold of the Memory Budget. Larger files are uploaded to /log with curl.

variables.name: Not Found Limit
variables.description: Lookups of unknown keys one client may make within the Not Found Window. Past that its lookups get 429 for the Not Found Ban time, which stops key guessing. An IPv6 client counts as its whole /64. Uploads still work. -1 turns it off.

variables.name: Not Found Window
variables.description: Seconds over which unknown key lookups are counted. 900 is 15 minutes.

variables.name: Not Found Ban
variables.description: Seconds a client IP that went over the Not Found Limit gets 429 on lookups. 3600 is one hour.

variables.name: GitHub Client ID
variables.description: Client ID of the GitHub OAuth App for login (preview, see Accounts in the README). Empty keeps login off. Set the app's callback URL to the Base URL followed by /auth/github/callback. Login needs an https Base URL.

variables.name: GitHub Client Secret
variables.description: Client secret of the GitHub OAuth App. Only panel admins can see or change it; the server never logs it or shows it.

variables.name: Accounts Database
variables.description: SQLite file for accounts and sessions. Empty means hastebin.db in the data folder with file storage, else in the server folder. It is created when login is turned on, with mode 0600.

variables.name: Session Lifetime
variables.description: Seconds a login lasts at most. 2592000 is 30 days.

variables.name: Session Idle Timeout
variables.description: Seconds a login lasts without being used. 604800 is 7 days.

variables.name: Admin GitHub IDs
variables.description: Numeric GitHub user ids of the admins, comma separated, for example 583231. Find yours at https://api.github.com/users/<login>. Admins get the /admin page.

variables.name: Admin Re-login
variables.description: Seconds after a login an admin may still take destructive actions without logging in again. 43200 is 12 hours.

variables.name: Minimum GitHub Account Age
variables.description: Seconds a GitHub account must exist before it can register, against throwaway accounts. 604800 is 7 days. Admins are exempt. -1 turns the check off.
